title: Evaluation of Factors Determining the Quality and Outcome of Out-of-Hospital and In-Hospital Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
summary: Cardiac arrest is associated with a severe clinical course and high mortality. A systematic evaluation of patients with cardiac arrest is therefore essential to improve our understanding of this condition. The Heidelberg Resuscitation Registry includes all patients with cardiac arrest in order to identify potential risk factors for increased mortality, poor neurological outcome, and a severe in-hospital course. Survival analyses are applied for this purpose. These analyses aim to identify risk factors that may influence patient outcome and could thus be investigated as therapeutic targets in future studies.

- Resuscitations in the cardiac catheterization laboratory
- Patients transferred to the hospital from the emergency physician’s catchment area after acute resuscitation

Exclusion criteria:
